summary: Defines the ORIGIN frame for HTTP/3. The frame already exists for HTTP/2 and applies equally well to HTTP/3, but it needs to be separately registered.

eli5.summary: A server tells your browser which websites it can speak for. HTTP/2 had this already, now HTTP/3 does too.

questions: how does a server list origins in http/3
what is the http/3 origin frame
what is frame type 0x0c in http/3
how does http/3 origin differ from http/2
subtitle: Registers the HTTP/2 ORIGIN frame for HTTP/3 so servers can list the origins a connection covers.

tldr.problem: The ORIGIN frame for HTTP/2 is equally applicable to HTTP/3, but HTTP/3 needs it registered separately.
tldr.mechanism: The ORIGIN frame is sent by the server on its control stream with the same payload as in HTTP/2: zero or more Origin-Entry fields, frame type 0x0c.
tldr.outcome: HTTP/3 servers can tell clients which origins a connection is or could be authoritative for. The RFC registers the frame type and adds no new security considerations.

today: RFC 9412 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Carrying ORIGIN Over to HTTP/3
sections.content:
Extensions defined for HTTP/2 often remain useful in HTTP/3, and Appendix A.2 of RFC 9114 describes the updates needed to use HTTP/2 frames with HTTP/3. RFC 8336 defines the HTTP/2 ORIGIN frame, which indicates what origins are available on a given connection. It defines a single frame type.

This RFC does the same for HTTP/3. The frame's meaning is unchanged, but the frame type must be registered for HTTP/3 on its own.
sections.eli5: A feature that worked on the old road also works on the new road, but the new road needs its own sign that lists it.

sections.title: The ORIGIN Frame and Its Layout
sections.content:
The ORIGIN frame lets a server indicate which origins it would like the client to consider as members of the Origin Set for the connection. The payload semantics are identical to HTTP/2. Where HTTP/2 sends the frame on stream 0, HTTP/3 sends it from the server to the client on the server's control stream. HTTP/3 has no Flags field and no flags are defined for ORIGIN, so none are carried.

The frame type is 0x0c (decimal 12), as in HTTP/2. The payload holds zero or more Origin-Entry fields. Each entry has Origin-Len, an unsigned 16-bit integer giving the length in octets of the next field, and ASCII-Origin, an OPTIONAL sequence of characters holding the ASCII serialization of an origin that the sender asserts this connection is or could be authoritative for.
sections.eli5: The server sends a list of website names. Each name is written with its length first so the browser knows where it ends.

sections.title: Security and IANA Registration
sections.content:
The RFC introduces no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 8336 and RFC 9114.

It registers one entry in the "HTTP/3 Frame Types" registry: value 0x0c, frame type ORIGIN, status permanent, dated 2023-03-14, change controller IETF, contact the HTTP WG.
sections.eli5: Nothing new to worry about. The only paperwork is writing the new frame in the official list.
